0.note: The word translated as **chief musician** likely refers to the person in charge of music for worship. Some languages may have a term for a music leader. Alternate translation: [For the music director] or [For the leader of worship music]
See how you translated the term **Gittith** in the superscription to Psalm 8.

1.note: The psalmist is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of amazement at the beauty of God’s dwelling place. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Your dwellings are so lovely]

2.note: The psalmist is using one part of himself, his **soul**, to mean all of himself in the act of longing. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I long and even faint]

The terms **longs** and **faints** mean similar things. The psalmist is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [desperately yearns]

The psalmist is speaking of **my heart and my flesh** as if they were living things that could **cry out**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my heart and my flesh groan loudly]

The psalmist is referring to all of himself by naming two major components, **my heart** and **my flesh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [with my whole being I]

Here, **my heart** represents the psalmist’s desires and feelings. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [my inner self]

3.note: The psalmist is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the swallow has found a nest for herself]

4.note: The psalmist is using a phrase **The happinesses of** that expresses a strong feeling of joy or blessing. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Oh, how happy are]
The psalmist is speaking of the temple of Yahweh as if it were a **house** in which he lived. Alternate translation: [your temple]

5.note: See how you translated the phrase “The happinesses of” in the previous verse.

The psalmist is not referring to a specific **man**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the person]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **strength**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [you make him strong]

The psalmist is speaking of the desire for pilgrimage as if there were **highways** in the hearts of the people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They desire to make the journey to your temple] or [Pilgrimage journeys are in their thoughts]

The pronoun **their** refers to the kind of person described as **the man** in the first part of the verse. The psalmist shifts from singular to plural because he is speaking of everyone who fits this description. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [are in his heart]

Here, **their heart** represents the desires and intentions of the people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [are in their thoughts]

6.note: The psalmist is speaking of the pilgrims as if they transformed the Valley of Baca into **a spring** of water. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they find water there] or [they make it a place of refreshment]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **blessings**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with good things from God]

7.note: The pronoun **They** refers to the pilgrims described in verses 5 and 6 who are traveling to God’s temple. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The pilgrims go]

The psalmist is using **from strength to strength** as a common expression meaning that the pilgrims grow increasingly strong as they travel. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [with ever-increasing strength]

8.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **prayer**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what I pray]

9.note: The psalmist is speaking of God as if he were a **shield** that protects in battle. If this image communicates well in your language, please use it. If not, you could express this as a comparison. Alternate translation: [our protector] or [the one who shields us]

Here, **the face** represents the person of the anointed king. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [your anointed one]

The psalmist is using the adjective **anointed** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [your anointed one]

10.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for the request made in verses 8 and 9. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because]

The psalmist says **than a thousand** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [than any number of days elsewhere]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **wickedness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the tents of wicked people]

Here, **the tents** represents the homes and dwellings of wicked people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the homes of wickedness]

11.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a further reason for the psalmist’s desire to be in God’s courts. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because]

The psalmist is speaking of Yahweh God as if he were **a sun** that gives life and light and **a shield** that protects from harm. If these images communicate well in your language, please use them. If not, you could express them as comparisons. Alternate translation: [the one who gives us life like the sun and protects us like a shield]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **favor** and **glory**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [treats people favorably and honors them]

The psalmist is using the adjective **good** as a noun to mean a certain kind of thing. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [good things]

The psalmist is speaking of how a person lives as if that were a path that the person was **walking** along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the ones living in blamelessness]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **blamelessness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [blamelessly]

12.note: The psalmist is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of joy or blessing. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [oh, how happy is]

The psalmist is not referring to a specific **man**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the person]
